sections.h2: Who bills the property tax in Miami?
sections.html:
The county tax collector mails the bill, working from values the county property appraiser sets. Miami adds its own mills to the same statement, next to county, school and special-district lines.

Miami spreads over 36.00 square miles and had about 489,812 residents in mid-2025, a rise of 10.8 percent since the 2020 base. With that much ground, parcels in different neighborhoods can fall on different taxing lines.

sections.h2: What does the 2026 adopted millage chart show for Miami?
sections.html:
The chart lists Miami at 7.1080 mills for city operations and 0.2536 for city debt service, for a total of 19.9544 mills. The county prints the title as 2026 adopted millage rates.

A separate line for the downtown development area adds 0.3800 and totals 20.3344. If your house is inside that boundary, your total is the second figure.

  • Check the parcel on the appraiser's site to see which line applies.
  • Miami's city line is higher than Coral Gables at 5.5590 and Miami Beach at 5.8060, so owners here carry more city mills than in either neighbor.
  • One mill equals one dollar of tax per thousand dollars of taxable value.

sections.h2: How does Miami compare with nearby municipalities on the chart?
sections.html:
Miami's total of 19.9544 mills is higher than Miami Beach at 18.6681, Coral Gables at 18.1518 and Hialeah at 18.6134. It is lower than Miami Gardens at 22.3393 and North Miami at 22.1081.

The spread comes almost entirely from the city line. Every row shares the same countywide, school and regional pieces, so moving across a city boundary changes the bill mainly through the municipal mills.

For a seller, that gap matters when buyers compare a Miami house against one a few miles away. Ask the title agent to show the exact folio total on the 2026 bill.

sections.h2: How large is Miami, and what drives its economy?
sections.html:
Miami counted 442,241 people in 2020, up from 399,457 in 2010, and it holds 12,285.8 people per square mile.

  • Foreign-born residents are 57.7 percent of the city.
  • Veterans number 7,305, and commutes average 27.3 minutes.
  • Among adults 25 and older, 81.3 percent finished high school and 37.4 percent hold a four-year degree.
  • For 2022 the Census lists about $17.0 billion in transportation and warehousing receipts, $13.2 billion in retail sales and $8.7 billion in health care revenue.

Those totals show how much of the city's economy runs through freight, health care and retail.

Owners occupy just 30.8 percent of Miami housing units. Owners put the typical home at $518,100, while renters pay a median of $1,758 gross.

The city counts 194,821 households. Median household income is $62,462 in 2024 dollars, and 19.4 percent of residents are in poverty.

Where renting dominates, many houses belong to investors. Homestead relief helps only a resident owner, so a landlord selling typically sees the full just-value assessment.

sections.h2: Which Miami property tax dates matter most?
sections.html:
Most of the cycle is set by state law, and the county adds its own offices and notices.

sections.h2: What should a Miami seller line up before closing?
sections.html:
A Miami closing goes faster when the paperwork is ready. Gather the items below before the title agent asks.

  • Your folio number, from the appraiser's parcel search or your latest bill.
  • The TRIM notice from August, which shows the proposed taxes and the date of the budget hearings.
  • Proof of any homestead, senior, widow(er) or veteran exemption on file.
  • A payoff letter from the tax collector if any year is still open.

If the house sits inside the downtown development area, tell the title agent, because that parcel carries the extra 0.3800 mills and a total of 20.3344 on the 2026 chart.

Buyers should also know that a Miami sale resets assessed value to just value the following January, so the first bill after closing can run well above the seller's.

sections.h2: How do I claim homestead on a Miami house?
sections.html:
Send Form DR-501 to the county property appraiser before March 1, and live in the home as your permanent residence on January 1. The appraiser also takes widow(er) and veteran disability exemption filings online.

The state describes up to $50,000 of exemption: $25,000 against every tax, plus a second slice that skips school taxes. Save Our Homes then holds yearly growth to the lower of 3 percent or CPI.

A rented house loses the exemption. Servicemembers get a narrow exception.

sections.h2: Can I move my Save Our Homes benefit when I leave a Miami house?
sections.html:
Possibly. Portability lets assessment savings follow you to a new Florida homestead, provided the new one starts within three years of the January 1 that follows abandoning the old. File Form DR-501T alongside the DR-501 by March 1.

Without it, a sale resets the buyer's assessed value to just value. The state names exceptions for spouses and certain transfers at death.

If a bill is hard to pay, deferral applications on Form DR-570 are due March 31, and installment requests May 1.

sections.h2: What if I owe back taxes on a Miami house?
sections.html:
Unpaid bills go delinquent on April 1, and the tax collector sells a certificate on the debt. State law has those sales done by June 1.

  • The holder cannot demand money from you for two years after April 1 of the issue year.
  • A tax deed application costs $75.
  • On a homestead parcel, the opening bid adds half of the latest assessed value.

A Miami seller with arrears can still close, because the title company clears the lien from proceeds. Request a payoff figure from the tax collector early.

sections.h2: What does a tax deed sale mean for a Miami owner?
sections.html:
When a certificate sits unpaid, the clerk can run a public auction. The top bidder posts a nonrefundable deposit, the larger of 5 percent of the bid or $200.

The tax collector lists who must receive notice: the titleholder, lienholders, mortgagees and contract-for-deed vendees. With no bidder, the land joins a list of lands available for taxes, and the county has 90 days to buy at the opening bid.

An owner who is behind should talk to the tax collector long before an auction is set, since a sale of the house normally clears the lien.

sections.h2: Where do Miami deeds get recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Miami-Dade County Recorder's Office at 20 NW 1st Avenue, Suite 5.246. The county clerk is the recorder for Miami addresses.

The clerk's checklist for deeds includes an original signature from the seller, two unrelated witnesses with printed names and addresses, a notary acknowledgement and a Prepared By line. Deed stamps run 60 cents per $100.

faqs.q: Is the Miami city millage rate 7.1080?
faqs.a: Yes, for city operations on the county's 2026 adopted chart, with 0.2536 more for city debt. All authorities together total 19.9544 mills, or 20.3344 on the downtown development line.

faqs.q: Can a Miami landlord claim homestead?
faqs.a: No. Homestead needs the owner to live there as a permanent residence by January 1, and renting the unit ends it.

faqs.q: What early-payment discounts apply to a Miami tax bill?
faqs.a: The schedule steps down monthly from 4 percent for November to 1 percent for February. March is due at the full amount.

faqs.q: Does the Miami property appraiser collect tax?
faqs.a: No. Its homepage says it neither sends bills nor sets or collects taxes. Pay the Miami-Dade tax collector.

faqs.q: How do I look up my Miami taxable value?
faqs.a: Search by address, owner name or folio on the property appraiser's site, or call 305-375-4712 to ask for an assessment review.
